title: Observability Weekly - 2026-05-04
summary: Weekly notes for Observability (tracing, dashboards, cost telemetry). Focus this week on tracing sampling adjustments, dashboard refresh for cost-per-token telemetry, and rollout plan for new latency percentile dashboards.
notes:
Meeting: Observability sync 2026-05-04 10:00-10:45 PT
Attendees: Aisha, Ben, Diego, Sofia, Grace, Jaidev (infra)

1) Tracing / Sampling
- Background: We saw 2.8x increase in trace ingestion during the Canary rollout on 2026-04-29; storage downstream costs and ingest CPU increased.
- Decision: Reduce default distributed tracing sampling for hosted-api to 0.5% for production traffic and keep 5% for error-sampled traces. Maintain 100% sampling for Dedicated staging clusters for debugging.
- Technical approach: Implement adaptive head-based sampling using Opentelemetry SDK extension. Head-sampler will keep high sampling for p95+ latency requests and for requests hitting fallback policies. Ben to prototype in feature branch and run load tests.
- Risks: Under-sampling could hide flaky rollout regressions. Plan to run short-term higher-sample windows around model rollouts (config flag controlled by console).

2) Dashboards / Latency Percentiles
- Work done: Diego finished migration of p50/p90/p95/p99 panels to the new metrics schema and removed deprecated metric aliases. Dashboards now use aggregated histograms from the RT collector.
- Next: Add colored threshold bands and an interactive time-range selector for rollout windows. Sofia to own UX copy and placement.
- Action: Create a lightweight overlay that shows which model version was serving during the selected window (requires linking routing metadata). Grace to follow up with Platform Engineering on metadata availability (see JIRA-OBS-342).

3) Cost Telemetry / Cost-per-token
- Observation: Preliminary cost telemetry shows a 12% increase in per-token GPU cost across dedicated pools last week; most of this is due to longer-context requests from a single enterprise customer during evening windows.
- Short-term: Add alert to notify when cost-per-token increases >10% over a rolling 7-day baseline for a customer pool. Set initial alert to notify #billing-alerts and obs-oncall.
- Long-term: Work on a per-route cost attribution pipeline using request tagging and the existing trace ID linkage. This will allow putting cost labels into the timeline and track model-level cost regressions.

4) Alerts and SLOs
- SLO review: p95 tail latency SLO for the hosted text generation route remains at 450ms; we saw 8 violations in the last 7 days mostly correlated with infra maintenance windows.
- Plan: Introduce temporary burn-rate suppression during planned infra maintenance and auto-suppress for known Dedicated maintenance windows. Jaidev to add suppression windows and document in the playbook.

5) Observability Platform Improvements
- Telemetry pipeline: Upgraded Kafka consumer group to use the new compacted topic for spans which reduced backpressure in dev clusters.
- SDK/working docs: Draft of "how we trace requests across Redwood" doc is in progress (linked in CON-OBS-1289). Please review if you haven't.

6) Ops / Incident follow-up
- Follow-up from 2026-04-29 Canary incident: root cause was an unbounded trace exporter retry loop. Fix deployed and validated; storage reclaim job run on 2026-05-01.
- Postmortem draft assigned to Diego (due 2026-05-08).
